answer:
**Hypothesis (data-grounded):** Within 2000–1100 BCE, the highest-growth phase was the **15th–14th centuries BCE, i.e. 1500–1401 BCE**, with the peak rate in the **15th century BCE (1500–1401)** and the strongest capital expansion in the **14th century BCE (1400–1301)**. All three independent growth signals — the study's primary openness/demographic growth proxy (`pollen_grate_100`), the KDE growth rate (`g_all_mean`), and century-on-century changes of the four documented capital categories — rank these two centuries first and second. Growth declines continuously after 1400 BCE and turns clearly negative in the 13th–12th centuries BCE (1300–1101 BCE), the weakest centuries in the window on all signals; this late-window contraction is consistent with (though not proof of) Late Bronze Age collapse dynamics, cited only as external context.

**Ranked century table (9 full centuries, bin BCE=X covers X..X−99; rank 1 = highest):**

| Century bin (BCE) | mean pollen_grate_100 (rank) | mean g_all_mean (rank) | ΔSymbolic | ΔSocial | ΔCultural | ΔEconomic | ΔAllCapital (rank) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1500–1401 | **+0.00189 (1)** | **+0.00283 (1)** | +0.05 | +0.15 | 0.00 | +0.27 | +0.14 (5) |
| 1400–1301 | **+0.00111 (2)** | **+0.00145 (2)** | **+0.75 (1)** | **+1.53 (1)** | 0.00 (2) | **+0.33 (1)** | **+0.68 (1)** |
| 1700–1601 | +0.00086 (3) | +0.00005 (6) | −1.77 (9) | +0.16 (2) | −0.21 (9) | −0.25 (7) | −0.52 (9) |
| 1900–1801 | +0.00017 (4) | +0.00028 (4) | +0.61 (3) | 0.00 (6) | −0.13 (8) | +0.10 (4) | +0.16 (4) |
| 1300–1201 | −0.00017 (5) | −0.00155 (8) | +0.01 | 0.00 | 0.00 | −0.84 (9) | −0.28 (7) |
| 1800–1701 | −0.00025 (6) | −0.00007 (7) | +0.60 (4) | +0.16 (3) | +0.13 (1) | +0.28 (2) | +0.30 (2) |
| 2000–1901 | −0.00090 (7) | +0.00007 (5) | +0.09 | −0.15 (8) | −0.05 (7) | 0.00 (6) | −0.02 (6) |
| 1200–1101 | −0.00104 (8) | −0.00437 (9) | −0.80 (8) | −0.21 (9) | 0.00 (2) | −0.40 (8) | −0.39 (8) |
| 1600–1501 | −0.00301 (9) | +0.00115 (3) | +0.74 (2) | +0.04 (5) | 0.00 (2) | +0.05 (5) | +0.21 (3) |

**Convergence/divergence:** `pollen_grate_100` and `g_all_mean` agree perfectly on the top two centuries (1500, 1400) and on the bottom (1200–1101 negative). Capital Δ co-peaks at 1400 BCE — driven by **Social capital** (Δ = +1.53, by far the largest category jump in the window) and Economic capital; the 15th c. leads on demographic/KDE growth while the 14th c. leads on capital accumulation, together forming one contiguous high-growth phase. The divergent century is 1600 BCE: worst on pollen growth but rank 2–3 on capital Δ and g_all_mean (its ΔSymbolic +0.74 is recovery after a −1.77 drop into 1700 BCE). The headline (1500–1401 BCE) is decided by the primary signal `pollen_grate_100` and is corroborated by the other two, so no divergence changes the answer.

**Sensitivity (smoothing choice):** Century means of the pct-change of SMOOTH_MEAN_100y from the raw pollen file (time-ascending) rank 1400 first and 1500 second; using absolute level change instead of pct, Top3 = [1400, 1500, 1900]. The 1600 BCE bin's pct value (−0.105) is a **division artifact** — the smoothed level crosses zero in 1522–1521 BCE — not real signal. A median-based century ranking of `pollen_grate_100` also gives 1500 > 1400 > 1700. The answer is not an artifact of one smoothing choice.

**Workflow:** loaded the three CSVs (comma decimals for capital/pollen files); window 2000–1100 BCE inclusive (901 annual rows, 0 missing in the four growth columns); binned annual rows onto the capital.csv century grid; computed century means of `pollen_grate_100` and `g_all_mean`; computed within-category means of the 12 capital Z-values (Symbolic/Social/Cultural/Economic per the documented grouping) and their century-on-century differences (ΔX = Z(X) − Z(X+100)); ranked all 9 centuries; ran the smoothing sensitivity from the raw pollen file.

**Limitations:** (i) bin BCE=2000 read as 2000–1901 BCE (capital.csv edge convention); (ii) the CE = −1100 endpoint year was assigned to its own '1100' bin and excluded from the 9-century ranking (its values are strongly negative, −0.0026/−0.0053, consistent with the 1200–1101 decline); (iii) the raw-pollen pct-change has a near-zero-denominator artifact in the 1600 BCE bin, handled via the absolute-change variant; (iv) Cultural capital Δ is identically 0 for 1500–1101 BCE (constant Z-values in capital.csv over that stretch), so it carries no discriminating information in the second half of the window; (v) Late Bronze Age / collapse framing is external context, not inferred from these files.

payload.hypothesis: The highest-growth phase of 2000-1100 BCE was the 15th-14th centuries BCE (1500-1401 BCE): the peak demographic/openness growth rate (pollen_grate_100) and KDE growth rate (g_all_mean) both occur in the 15th century BCE (1500-1401), immediately followed by the strongest capital expansion in the 14th century BCE (1400-1301), led by Social capital (Delta +1.53) and Economic capital. Growth then declines through the 13th century and is clearly negative in the 12th century BCE (1200-1101 BCE), the weakest period in the window on all signals.
payload.workflow: Loaded time_series_data.csv, capital.csv (comma decimals) and the Belau/Woserin pollen openness file; restricted to 2000-1100 BCE inclusive (901 annual rows, zero missing values in kde_all_mean, g_all_mean, pollen_inter_100, pollen_grate_100); binned annual data onto the capital.csv century grid (bin BCE=X covers X..X-99; CE=-1100 endpoint isolated); computed century means of pollen_grate_100 (primary growth signal) and g_all_mean (corroborating KDE growth); built four documented capital category indices (Symbolic, Social, Cultural, Economic) and pooled AllCapital from within-category means of the 12 Z columns and computed century-on-century deltas Z(X)-Z(X+100); ranked all 9 centuries by each signal; sensitivity check via pct-change and absolute level change of SMOOTH_MEAN_100y from the raw pollen file (time-ascending; zero-crossing artifact in the 1600 BCE bin identified and excluded from interpretation).
